hmmt-feb-2026-geo-01.title: Congruent right triangles
hmmt-feb-2026-geo-01.body:
Let $P$ be the foot from $Y$ to $AB$. Since $\angle WXY=90^\circ$, $\angle AWX=90^\circ-\angle AXW=\angle PXY$; also $\angle WAX=\angle XPY=90^\circ$ and $WX=XY$. So $\triangle WAX\cong\triangle XPY$, giving $XP=AW=4$ (and $PY=AX=5$). Then $PB=12-5-4=3$, which is the distance from $Y$ to $BC$. Area $=\frac12\cdot12\cdot3=18$.

**Answer: 18**

hmmt-feb-2026-geo-01.title: Coordinates
hmmt-feb-2026-geo-01.body:
$A=(0,0)$, $B=(12,0)$, $D=(0,12)$, $W=(0,4)$, $X=(5,0)$. Rotating $\overrightarrow{XW}=(-5,4)$ by $-90^\circ$ gives $\overrightarrow{XY}=(4,5)$, so $Y=(9,5)$ (inside the square). Its distance to $BC$ ($x=12$) is $3$, so $[BCY]=\frac12\cdot12\cdot3=18$.

**Answer: 18**

hmmt-feb-2026-geo-02.title: Trapezoid plus a right triangle
hmmt-feb-2026-geo-02.body:
$HO\parallel ES$ (both perpendicular to $HE$), so $HOSE$ is a right trapezoid. Let $O_1$ be the foot from $O$ to $SE$: $O_1S=26-20=6$, so $HE=OO_1=\sqrt{100-36}=8$ and $[HOSE]=\frac{(20+26)\cdot8}2=184$.

Enclose the pentagon in rectangle $HXYE$ with $R$ on side $XY$ (parallel to $HE$). The $135^\circ$ angles make $\triangle OXR$ and $\triangle RYS$ isosceles right triangles; let $OX=XR=a$, $RY=YS=b$. Then $a-b=O_1S=6$ and $a+b=XY=HE=8$, so $a=7$, $b=1$. Thus $OR=7\sqrt2$, $RS=\sqrt2$, and the right triangle $ORS$ has area $\frac12\cdot7\sqrt2\cdot\sqrt2=7$.

Total $184+7=191$.

**Answer: 191**

hmmt-feb-2026-geo-02.title: Coordinates
hmmt-feb-2026-geo-02.body:
$H=(0,0)$, $O=(20,0)$, $E=(0,8)$, $S=(26,8)$ (as $OS=10$). Going from $O$ at $45^\circ$: $R=(27,7)$, and $RS$ goes at $135^\circ$ to $S$. Check $\angle ORS$: $\overrightarrow{RO}=(-7,-7)$, $\overrightarrow{RS}=(-1,1)$, dot product $0$ ✓. Shoelace on $H,O,R,S,E$: $\frac12\left[(0\cdot0-20\cdot0)+(20\cdot7-27\cdot0)+(27\cdot8-26\cdot7)+(26\cdot8-0\cdot8)+(0\cdot0-0\cdot8)\right]=\frac12(140+34+208)=191$.

**Answer: 191**

hmmt-feb-2026-geo-03.title: Centre and similar triangles
hmmt-feb-2026-geo-03.body:
Let $O$ be the intersection of the rhombus's diagonals. $OW=OY$ with $W\in AB$, $Y\in CD$ and $WY$ passing through $O$ means $O$ is equidistant from $AB$ and $CD$; similarly from $BC$ and $DA$. So $O$ is the centre of the rectangle.

Let $M,N$ be the midpoints of $AB,AD$: $OM=8$, $ON=6$. Since $OW\perp OZ$ and $OM\perp ON$, $\triangle OMW\sim\triangle ONZ$, so $OW:OZ=8:6$. Write $OW=4x$, $OZ=3x$: the diagonals are $8x,6x$, and $\frac12\cdot8x\cdot6x=120$ gives $x=\sqrt5$. The side is $\sqrt{(4x)^2+(3x)^2}=5x=5\sqrt5$.

**Answer: $5\sqrt5$**

hmmt-feb-2026-geo-04.title: Power of a point twice
hmmt-feb-2026-geo-04.body:
The circle $\omega$ centred at $T$ with radius $\ell$ passes through $A,X,Y$; since $T\in AC\perp AB$, it is tangent to $AB$ at $A$. Power of $B$: $BA^2=BX\cdot BY=4\cdot9$, so $BA=6$ and $AC=\sqrt{144-36}=6\sqrt3$.

Let $Z$ be the antipode of $A$ on $\omega$ (on line $AC$, with $AZ=2\ell$). Power of $C$: $CY\cdot CX=CZ\cdot CA$, i.e. $3\cdot8=(6\sqrt3-2\ell)\cdot6\sqrt3$, so $6\sqrt3-2\ell=\frac{4}{\sqrt3}$ and $\ell=3\sqrt3-\frac2{\sqrt3}=\frac{7\sqrt3}3$.

**Answer: $\frac{7\sqrt3}{3}$**

hmmt-feb-2026-geo-04.title: Coordinates
hmmt-feb-2026-geo-04.body:
With $BA=6$ as above, put $A=(0,0)$, $B=(6,0)$, $C=(0,6\sqrt3)$ and $T=(0,\ell)$. $X$ is $\frac4{12}$ of the way from $B$ to $C$: $X=(4,2\sqrt3)$. $TX=TA$ gives $16+(2\sqrt3-\ell)^2=\ell^2$, so $28=4\sqrt3\,\ell$, $\ell=\frac{7}{\sqrt3}=\frac{7\sqrt3}3$. (Check with $Y=(\frac32,\frac{9\sqrt3}2)$: $\frac94+(\frac{9\sqrt3}2-\ell)^2=\ell^2$ gives the same $\ell$.)

**Answer: $\frac{7\sqrt3}{3}$**

hmmt-feb-2026-geo-05.title: Triangle of centres
hmmt-feb-2026-geo-05.body:
Let $A,B,C$ be the small circles' centres; $OA=OB=OC=11-2=9$, so $O$ is the circumcentre of $\triangle ABC$. A chord tangent to the circles at $A$ and $B$ is parallel to $AB$ at distance $2$ (on the side towards $O$).

A chord of length $4\sqrt{30}$ is at distance $\sqrt{121-120}=1$ from $O$. Say the chords along $AB$ and $AC$ have this length; then $O$ is at distance $1+2=3$ from lines $AB$ and $AC$, i.e. $OZ=OY=3$ where $Z,Y$ are the midpoints of $AB,AC$. So $AZ=AY=\sqrt{81-9}=6\sqrt2$ and $AB=AC=12\sqrt2$.

Let $X$ be the midpoint of $BC$; $A,O,X$ are collinear. $\triangle AZO\sim\triangle AXB$ gives $\frac{AZ}{AO}=\frac{AX}{AB}$: $\frac{6\sqrt2}{9}=\frac{9+OX}{12\sqrt2}$, so $OX=7$. The third chord is at distance $7-2=5$ from $O$, with length $2\sqrt{121-25}=8\sqrt6$.

**Answer: $8\sqrt6$**

hmmt-feb-2026-geo-05.title: Check with coordinates
hmmt-feb-2026-geo-05.body:
Put $O$ at the origin and $A=(0,9)$. $AB$ makes an angle $\theta$ with $AO$ where $\cos\theta=\frac{AZ}{AO}=\frac{2\sqrt2}{3}$ and $\sin\theta=\frac13$, so $B=A+12\sqrt2(-\sin\theta,-\cos\theta)=(-4\sqrt2,-7)$ and $C=(4\sqrt2,-7)$. Indeed $|OB|=\sqrt{32+49}=9$ ✓, line $BC$ is $y=-7$, the chord is $y=-5$, of length $2\sqrt{121-25}=8\sqrt6$.

**Answer: $8\sqrt6$**

hmmt-feb-2026-geo-06.title: $BP=CQ$ and power of a point
hmmt-feb-2026-geo-06.body:
**Claim: $BP=CQ$.** $\angle BPM+\angle MQC=360^\circ-(\angle B+\angle PMB)-(\angle C+\angle QMC)=360^\circ-(\angle A+\angle B+\angle C)=180^\circ$, so the sines are equal. By the Law of Sines in $\triangle BPM$ and $\triangle CQM$: $BP=\frac{BM\sin\angle PMB}{\sin\angle BPM}=\frac{CM\sin\angle QMC}{\sin\angle MQC}=CQ$.

Also $\angle PMQ=180^\circ-\angle A$, so $APMQ$ is cyclic. Let this circle meet $BC$ again at $T$. With $x=BP=CQ$, power of $B$ and $C$:
$$x(x+1)+x(x+3)=BT\cdot BM+CT\cdot CM=4(BT+CT)=32.$$
So $x^2+2x-16=0$, $x=\sqrt{17}-1$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{17}-1$**

hmmt-feb-2026-geo-06.title: Angle bisector
hmmt-feb-2026-geo-06.body:
Let $T$ be the foot of the bisector from $A$, and $a=8,b=AC,c=AB$. $\triangle BPM\sim\triangle BTA$ (common angle $B$, and $\angle PMB=\angle TAB=\frac A2$), so $BP=\frac{BM\cdot BT}{BA}=\frac{4\cdot\frac{8c}{b+c}}{c}=\frac{32}{b+c}$; similarly $CQ=\frac{32}{b+c}$. Then $AP=c-\frac{32}{b+c}=1$ and $AQ=b-\frac{32}{b+c}=3$ give $b=c+2$ and $c-\frac{32}{2c+2}=1$, i.e. $c^2=17$. So $BP=c-1=\sqrt{17}-1$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{17}-1$**

hmmt-feb-2026-geo-07.title: Reflect $B$ across $AP$
hmmt-feb-2026-geo-07.body:
Let $X$ be the reflection of $B$ across $AP$. Then $AX=AB=AC$ and $\angle PAX=20^\circ$, so $\angle XAQ=46^\circ-20^\circ=26^\circ=\angle QAC$. Hence $\triangle AXQ\cong\triangle ACQ$ and $X$ is also the reflection of $C$ across $AQ$. Therefore $PX=PB=PQ$ and $QX=QC=PQ$: $\triangle PQX$ is equilateral.

$Q$ is equidistant from $P,X,C$, so it is the circumcentre of $\triangle PXC$ and $\angle PCX=\frac12\angle PQX=30^\circ$. Since $XC\perp AQ$, $\angle ACX=90^\circ-26^\circ=64^\circ$, so $\angle ACP=64^\circ-30^\circ=34^\circ$. With $\angle PAC=46^\circ+26^\circ=72^\circ$:
$$\angle APC=180^\circ-72^\circ-34^\circ=74^\circ.$$

**Answer: $74^\circ$**

hmmt-feb-2026-geo-07.title: Rotate $\triangle APB$
hmmt-feb-2026-geo-07.body:
Let $P'$ be outside the triangle with $\triangle AP'C\cong\triangle APB$ (rotate about $A$ by $\angle BAC$). Then $\angle QAP'=26^\circ+20^\circ=46^\circ=\angle PAQ$ and $AP'=AP$, so $\triangle APQ\cong\triangle AP'Q$ and $P'Q=PQ=QC$. Also $P'C=PB=QC$, so $\triangle QP'C$ is equilateral, and $Q$ is the circumcentre of $\triangle PP'C$. Then $\angle APC=\angle APP'+\angle P'PC=(90^\circ-46^\circ)+\frac12\cdot60^\circ=74^\circ$.

**Answer: $74^\circ$**

hmmt-feb-2026-geo-08.title: Reflect to the circumcircle, then Ptolemy
hmmt-feb-2026-geo-08.body:
The circle $(ABH)$ is the reflection of $(ABC)$ through the midpoint of $AB$ (both have the same radius and chord $AB$, on opposite sides). Let $P'$ be the reflection of $P$ through the midpoint of $AB$; it lies on $(ABC)$, with $BP'=AP=4$ and $BP'\parallel AM$. Similarly $Q'$ (reflection of $Q$ through the midpoint of $AC$) is on $(ABC)$ with $CQ'=5$ and $CQ'\parallel AM$.

So $P'B\parallel Q'C$, making $BCQ'P'$ an isosceles trapezoid inscribed in the circle: $P'Q'=BC=7$. Moreover, since $CQ'\parallel AM$, the inscribed angle $\angle BCQ'$ equals the angle between lines $BC$ and $AM$, which is $\angle ACB+\frac12\angle BAC=\angle ACB+\angle BCM=\angle ACM$; equal inscribed angles give equal chords, so $BQ'=AM$. Similarly $CP'=AM$. Ptolemy on $BCQ'P'$:
$$BP'\cdot CQ'+BC\cdot P'Q'=BQ'\cdot CP'\implies20+49=AM^2,$$
so $AM=\sqrt{69}$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{69}$**

hmmt-feb-2026-geo-08.title: Reflect across the sides
hmmt-feb-2026-geo-08.body:
$(ABH)$ is also the reflection of $(ABC)$ across line $AB$. Reflect $P$ across $AB$ to $P'$ and $Q$ across $AC$ to $Q'$, both on $(ABC)$, with $AP'=4$, $AQ'=5$. Since $AM$ bisects $\angle BAC$, $\angle P'AM=\angle BAC=\angle MAQ'$, so $P'M=MQ'=BC=7$. In cyclic quadrilateral $AP'MQ'$, $\angle AP'M+\angle AQ'M=180^\circ$, so by the Law of Cosines
$$AM^2=16+49-56\cos\angle AP'M=25+49+70\cos\angle AP'M.$$
Eliminating the cosine: $126\,AM^2=70\cdot65+56\cdot74$, so $AM^2=\frac{4550+4144}{126}=69$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{69}$**

hmmt-feb-2026-geo-09.title: Radical axis is a midline
hmmt-feb-2026-geo-09.body:
Let the incircle touch $BC,CA,AB$ at $P,Q,R$. Circles $(CPIQ)$ (diameter $CI$), $(BIC)$ and $\omega$ have pairwise radical axes $CI$, $EF$ and $PQ$, which concur; $CI$ meets $PQ$ at its midpoint, so $EF$ passes through the midpoint of $PQ$. Similarly it passes through the midpoint of $PR$: $EF$ is the $P$-midline of $\triangle PQR$.

$\Gamma$ is tangent to $AB,AC$ with twice the radius, so it is the image of $\omega$ under the homothety at $A$ with ratio $2$; it touches $AC,AB$ at $Q',R'$ with $AQ'=2AQ$, $AR'=2AR$. The radical axis $EF$ of $\omega$ and $\Gamma$ passes through the midpoints of $QQ'$ and $RR'$ (equal tangent lengths), so $EF$ is midway between lines $QR$ and $Q'R'$. Since $EF$ is also midway between $QR$ and $P$, $P$ lies on $Q'R'$.

Let $BC=x$; $s=\frac{12+x}2$, $AQ=s-x=6-\frac x2$, so $AQ'=AR'=12-x$; $BP=s-7=\frac x2-1$, $CP=\frac x2+1$. Menelaus on $\triangle ABC$ with line $R'PQ'$:
$$\frac{AR'}{R'B}\cdot\frac{BP}{PC}\cdot\frac{CQ'}{Q'A}=1\implies\frac{12-x}{7-x}\cdot\frac{x-2}{x+2}\cdot\frac{x-5}{12-x}=1,$$
which simplifies to $x^2-6x-2=0$, so $BC=3+\sqrt{11}$.

**Answer: $3+\sqrt{11}$**

hmmt-feb-2026-geo-10.title: Ratios along the median
hmmt-feb-2026-geo-10.body:
Let $H$ be the orthocentre of $\triangle AGO$ (on $BC$), $P$ the foot from $O$ to line $AG$ (the median $AM$), $M$ the midpoint of $BC$. The altitude of $\triangle AGO$ from $O$ is line $OP$, so $O,P,H$ are collinear. Since $H\in BC$ and $OM\perp BC$, triangle $OMH$ is right-angled at $M$ with altitude $MP$ (as $MP\perp OH$), so $PM^2=PO\cdot PH$. Also $AH\perp OG$ and $AP\perp OP$ give $\angle PAH=\angle POG$, so the right triangles $POG$ and $PAH$ are similar and $PO\cdot PH=PG\cdot PA$. So $PM^2=PG\cdot PA$.

Using $AM=3GM$: $3(PM+PG)=PA+PM$, so $2PM=PA-3PG$. Then $(PA-3PG)^2=4PG\cdot PA$, i.e. $PA^2-10PA\cdot PG+9PG^2=0$, so $PA=9PG$ (not $PA=PG$), and then $PM^2=9PG^2$ gives $AP=3PM$.

Let $PM=\ell$, $AP=3\ell$. $P$ is the midpoint of the chord $AA'$ along the median, so $AA'=6\ell$ and $MA'=2\ell$. Power of $M$: $MB^2=MA\cdot MA'=4\ell\cdot2\ell=8\ell^2$. The median formula: $AB^2+AC^2=2(AM^2+MB^2)=2(16+8)\ell^2=48\ell^2$, so
$$BC^2=4MB^2=32\ell^2=\tfrac23(AB^2+AC^2)=\tfrac23(121+169)=\tfrac{580}3.$$

**Answer: $\sqrt{\frac{580}{3}}$**

hmmt-feb-2026-geo-10.title: Coordinate check
hmmt-feb-2026-geo-10.body:
With $B=(0,0)$, $C=(a,0)$ and $AB=11$, $AC=13$, computing $G$, $O$ and the orthocentre of $AGO$ for $a=\sqrt{580/3}\approx13.904$ gives an orthocentre with $y$-coordinate $0$ (to machine precision), i.e. on $BC$. In general the condition is equivalent to $BC^2=\frac23(AB^2+AC^2)$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{\frac{580}{3}}$**
